calls.head: The Red Wings can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Red Wings’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Rangers’ power play is near the top of the league. Discipline matters more than usual for the Red Wings tonight.
calls.call: The Rangers’ power play creates at least their usual 7.8 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: NY Rangers 9th for power play (7.8 expected goals per 60) · Detroit 23rd for penalty kill

calls.happened: NY Rangers’s power play created 5.6 expected goals per 60 in 7:41 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 7.8, and scored 1 goal.

calls.head: Forecheck against patience
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, the Rangers is one of the league’s best and Detroit is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Rangers put more forecheck pressure on than the Red Wings.

surprises.head: Detroit tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Copp, A. DeBrincat, L. Raymond played 14:09 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Detroit’s usual lines.

surprises.head: NY Rangers shut down Detroit’s power play
surprises.body: Detroit’s power play created 3.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.6 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Garand shuts out the Red Wings
paras: Sean Durzi opened the scoring early in the first. Dylan Garand stopped all 22 shots.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Red Wings tried a line they hadn’t used before: Andrew Copp, Alex DeBrincat and Lucas Raymond.

items.text: Whether the Red Wings keep that line together at home against Winnipeg on Sunday.
None of the preview’s two calls held.
